provider: Absolute Title, LLC ("New England's Premier Title Company" -- independent title company, offices in NH/ME/MA including Lowell, MA)
endpoint: No HTTP endpoint -- entirely client-side JS. scenario: $500,000 purchase price, $400,000 loan, statewide MA pricing (no county selector in this calculator -- Absolute Title's own MA office is in Lowell, Middlesex County), residential purchase transaction, not simultaneous issue, not Nantucket, not condo, not new construction
methodology: Found via web search for MA title-insurance rate calculators. View-source of ratecalculator_ma.asp revealed a first-party (non-platform) JS calculator at rc-ma.js with all fee logic as literal constants/formulas (getPremium(), getOwnersPremium(), getLPremium()) -- fetched the JS directly and hand-reproduced its arithmetic in Python for the standard scenario rather than executing it in a browser, since the logic is pure client-side math with no server round-trip.

bundlingNotes: Genuine first-party, non-platform calculator (not TitleCapture/Qualia/MyTitleRates/CATICulator) -- a small independent New England title company's own hand-rolled JS, same discovery pattern as Modern Title Group (MI) documented in CALCULATORS.md. Settlement Fee and Plot Plan are flat provider-set fees; CPL and Wire are flat static fees embedded directly in the page HTML (not computed); the title insurance premium math (loan and owner policy) is a per-thousand formula with a minimum floor, structured as a simultaneous-issue-style combined rate (owner's policy priced as an incremental add-on to the loan policy premium) distinct from Stewart's separately-tiered Standard/Enhanced tables already on file in this state's premium rate-card section above.
transactionContext: Calculator-derived point estimate for the standard $500k/$400k statewide MA purchase scenario, standard (non-Nantucket, non-simultaneous) residential purchase.

provider: The Law Office of David R. Rocheford, Jr., P.C. ("The Best Closings") -- Massachusetts closing attorney, Leominster, MA (Worcester County)
endpoint: No HTTP endpoint -- entirely client-side JS. The page loads a WordPress plugin script at https://www.thebestclosings.com/wp-content/plugins/title-loan-calculator/js/title-loan-calculator.php?ver=1.7, which contains hardcoded fee constants and formulas (basebuyerpays=1695, basesellerpays=345, lenderstitleins=(loanamount/1000)*2.75, ownerstitleins=(saleprice/1000)*4+175-lenderstitleins, transfertax=saleprice/1000*4.56) -- reproduced directly in Python, no browser/JS execution needed. Static (pre-calculation) per-line-item fee constants are also directly readable in the page's own HTML table.
scenario: $500,000 purchase price, $400,000 loan, statewide MA pricing (no county selector in this calculator -- firm is based in Leominster, Worcester County), residential purchase transaction
methodology: Found via web search for MA closing-attorney fee/title calculators. View-source of the title-calc page revealed a static HUD-1-style itemized fee table (Buyer Pays / Seller Pays columns) with most line items as fixed dollar constants directly in the page HTML, plus 3 computed line items (owner's title insurance, lender's title insurance, transfer tax) whose formulas are in the linked title-loan-calculator.php JS file -- both sources combined give the full itemized result for the standard scenario without needing to execute JS in a browser.

bundlingNotes: The richest single itemization found in this MA calculator-harvest session -- a genuine first-party, non-platform calculator built by a Massachusetts closing attorney's own website (WordPress "title-loan-calculator" plugin, not a national platform), directly consistent with MA.md's market-structure finding that closing attorneys ARE the settlement-fee-charging party in this state. Unlike Absolute Title's calculator above, this tool breaks out title exam, survey, MLC (twice, in two different fee buckets), overnight/wire fees, and recording separately from a standalone Settlement Fee line, and separately discloses buyer-side vs. seller-side allocation for every line item (MA convention: buyer pays title insurance/recording, seller pays transfer tax/discharge). No county tiering -- statewide MA flat-fee schedule from a Worcester County (Leominster) firm.
transactionContext: Calculator-derived point estimate for the standard $500k/$400k statewide MA purchase scenario, both buyer-side and seller-side fee allocations as displayed by the tool.
